title: Hybrid prefetch pagination + typed streaming for embeddings client
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a cross-language (Python + TypeScript) client upgrade for embeddings that combines a hybrid prefetching pagination model with typed streaming envelopes and improved error taxonomy. Goals: reduce tail latency for large multi-page requests, make client consumers strongly typed and ergonomic, and improve retry behavior to avoid duplicate scoring during reranking flows.
tasks: Design hybrid prefetch algorithm (leader: Marco) with configurable window and lookahead size
Define typed streaming envelope schema for embeddings responses (Python dataclasses + TS interfaces)
Implement async prefetch iterator in Python client (aio/iterator + backpressure hooks)
Implement prefetch + stream adapter in TS client (Node fetch + AbortSignal integration)
Add error classification layer: transient vs permanent vs throttling (map to HTTP codes and SDK exceptions)
Introduce idempotency tokens and best-effort deduplication for rerank scoring flows
Add end-to-end benchmarks against current SDK for 1k, 10k, 100k vectors with various page sizes
Add unit/integration tests for pagination boundaries, mid-stream errors, and resume semantics
Document migration guide and new typed API surface for both languages
Open PRs, get reviews, and coordinate rollout with product/SDK owners
acceptance_criteria: Python and TypeScript SDKs expose a new paginated iterator with optional prefetch window and a typed streaming envelope
End-to-end median latency for multi-page embedding requests reduced by >= 20% vs baseline for the 10k vector workload
Retry policy avoids double-scoring at the client by using idempotency tokens or deduplication where possible
All new public types are documented and exported; existing client surface is backwards compatible or has clear deprecation
Comprehensive test coverage: pagination edge cases, mid-stream cancellation, partial failures, and resume behavior
Benchmarks published in the embeddings SLO dashboard and linked in PR
comments: 2025-02-18 Aisha P: Kicked off spike to prototype prefetch window sizes. Found that a 2-page lookahead gives best median latency in our lab runs for typical 2-16 token-per-request workloads.

2025-02-21 Marco R: Implemented Python async iterator prototype. Early numbers: prefetch window=2 reduced tail latency by ~18% on 10k vector workload but increased CPU usage ~6% per request. Need to validate memory trade-offs for large page_size.
2025-02-25 Design review: agreed on typed streaming envelope shape: {meta, items[], warnings[], continuation_token}. Added 'source_model' to per-item meta for reranking explainability.
2025-02-27 QA: Failure mode test — server returns HTTP 503 mid-stream. Client resumes with continuation token and deduplication key; test passed for Python prototype.
2025-02-28 Marco R: Opened draft PR with Python and TS changes. Awaiting eng review. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1247
2025-03-01 Aisha P: PM review — ensure we surface throttling as a distinct exception so console can map to quotas and show actionable hints. Added to tasks.
links: Playbook note about reranking dedup: https://docs.redwood.ai/rerank-dedup
migration_notes: Existing consumer code using the current .paginate() helper will continue to work but will get a deprecation warning when using the old untyped iterator
New API: .paginate(prefetch_window=2, page_size=128, typed_stream=true) returns an async iterator of TypedEnvelope objects. Migration guide included in SDK release notes.
For rerank flows where downstream scoring must be idempotent, consumers should pass client-generated idempotency_key per query (examples included).
observability: Emit tracing spans for page_fetch and stream_resume with attributes: request_id, page_index, prefetch_window
Add dashboard panel that correlates prefetch_window to median and p95 latency broken out by consumer tier
testing_plan: Unit tests for typed envelope serialization/deserialization in both languages
Integration tests that spin up a local embeddings test server and simulate mid-stream failures and throttles
Load tests running the 1000/10000/100000 vector scenarios and comparing median/p95 token latencies vs baseline
Canary release to 5% of SDK users with opt-in flag; monitor error rates and latency regressions for 72 hours
rollout_plan: Merge PR -> publish SDK beta packages (python/ts) under `@redwood/sdk-beta` and `redwood-sdk-beta`
Invite 3 internal teams (search, rerank, knowledge-ops) to try beta and provide feedback within 10 days
If no major issues, promote to stable with minor bump and include migration guide in release notes
Coordinate with console team to show a tooltip about typed streaming in the SDK docs tab
